$comment: TF-C92 fold — the ELF half of the shipped <sys/ioctl.h> request-ENCODING macros, and the FIRST place any elf ioctl VALUE is computed. The `shipped_ioctl_iowr_macho` sibling pins Darwin's numbers with _Static_assert; the elf arms of the same four `when:{format}` rows were pinned only as `replacement` TEXT (tests/ffi/test_shipped_lib_descriptor.cpp string-compares them), so a shift/mask/direction error that preserved the text shape was undetected. Pins the exact values, MEASURED differentially by compiling each expression against the REAL musl arch/generic/bits/ioctl.h on disk with the host /usr/bin/clang: _IOR(0xf5,12,u32)=0x8004f50c, _IO(0xf5,1)=0xf501, _IOW(0xf5,13,u32)=0x4004f50d — all three PUBLISHED Linux F2FS_IOC_* constants, an independent witness that musl's formula was transcribed right, and 0xf5 is the magic sqlite writes on this arm (os_unix.c:392-396) — plus the derived _IOWR('z',23,struct ByteRangeLockPB2)=0xc0207a17, and SZ(struct/union/enum) for the sizeof-through-a-macro-param shape. ★ THE PER-FORMAT SELECTION IS PINNED, NOT JUST THE ROW: elf and macho encode the DIRECTION FIELD with OPPOSITE SENSE (Darwin IOC_OUT 0x40000000 = read vs Linux _IOC_READ 2 = 0x80000000), so the asserts include explicit `!= <macho value>` lines for _IOR/_IOW/_IO — a copy-paste between the two arms swaps read and write while both replacement strings still look plausible. _IOWR alone CANNOT witness the selection (0xc0207a17 is byte-identical on both formats, since IOC_INOUT and dir-code 3 both land on 0xc0000000); that coincidence is documented in main.c so it is not mistaken for a discriminator. ★ THE `u` SUFFIX IS **NOT** GUARDED HERE, AND THAT IS MEASURED, NOT AN OVERSIGHT — dropping it is invisible from inside a DSS-compiled TU: DSS does not sign-extend the overflowed `2 << 30` (MEASURED: `(unsigned long)(2 << 30) == 0x80000000ul` passes, and both spellings of the _IOR body fold to the same 0x8004f50c), and the _IO signedness probe that would otherwise work rests on unsigned wraparound, which DSS's constant evaluator gets WRONG (`0u - 1u == 0xffffffffu` fails under DSS, passes under clang — reported as its own defect). What these asserts DO guard: that DSS computes the number host clang computes from the real header. HOST REALITY: elf-only targets with runOn linux, so the macOS dev host COMPILES both arms (every value pin is a compile-time _Static_assert, load-bearing there) and reports SkippedCrossHost for the run; the Linux CI leg runs main and re-checks the same numbers through the real `unsigned long` request parameter of a variadic libc ioctl on fd -1 (EBADF, no side effect). BOTH elf arches are listed deliberately — `when` is FORMAT-only by construction, so x86_64 and arm64 must agree, which is the witness for that claim in sys/ioctl.json's ARCH CAVEAT. exit 42 iff the elf macro variants were selected AND their encodings match the native header. Release arm runs the optimizer over the folded encodings + the variadic call.
